note: Not assessable. Internal call between the closer and his setter with no prospect present, so there is nobody to judge against the ICP criteria; fit is left null rather than forced into core, edge or outside. It should be read alongside the assessments rather than counted as one, because it explains how the income criterion is actually being applied in practice: by asking ChatGPT what a job title pays. Of a commercial diver — 'when I put that into ChatGPT, it said he was probably making around 75k, around there' — and of a 23-year-old firefighter, 'I once again chat GPT'd, like, estimated salary for a five-year firefighter, and it said that would be around 60k.' Occupation is being used as a proxy for ability to pay, which is exactly the substitution the stated ICP invites, since 'successful' and 'makes good money' are listed as separate criteria but only the first is observable from a job title. Every miss on income in this batch was invisible to that method: a school counsellor on over six figures with zero liquidity, an accountant with two mortgages and a $1,000/month ceiling, a veteran on disability with five children, and a retired music teacher who expected to pay $30 a month. The same call also records a lead being booked despite known low intent, and a prospect reaching a closing call with an acutely injured back because nobody asks whether a prospect is able to train.
